### Stage #1 Reflection 

The overarching theme of our group is the cause and effect of prisons and their geography. Collectively we took an interest in things such as gerrymandering, regional differences, and how the location of correctional facilities impact the surrounding area. Across Rae, Jessie, and Hayden’s work rural towns and economies are especially relevant; prison gerrymandering typically shifts representation from urban areas to rural settings, which is due to the placement of prisons in primarily rural areas; such placement is within the scope of Jessie’s investigation, while Hayden will have the chance to explore how members of rural communities react/are impacted by the presence of prisons. In short, Jessie will investigate why a prison is placed where it is, Rae will look at the state and national political implications of that placement, while Hayden will explore the immediate local and social effects of prisons’ locations. Kayla narrows that down into examining the effects on how, specifically, Black individuals are treated within the legal system through regional differences.

We’ve started to compile a list of relevant pieces of literature to our topics and have already started to see certain overlaps. We’re hoping that these similarities will also be helpful when it comes to looking for datasets. While Jessie is looking at the cause and reasoning behind prison locations, Hayden is focusing on the effect that these placements have on the greater community. Kayla is also taking a comparative approach by looking at regional differences. Hayden’s and Rae’s work will mutually support one another; since representation is, ultimately, a highly social concept, with far reaching societal impacts, we suspect that Hayden’s research may touch upon the feelings of those community members whose representation is diluted/enhanced by the presence of a prison. This in turn can lead to mutual exchange between Rae and Hayden. Finally, we all want to make sure that we represent the people behind and within these systems, so we will all have a dependence on demographic and interpersonal information.
